Score an imputation model on reference rows it did not see

Source: R/contamination.R
catmech_holdout_check.Rd

Hides folds of reference values, refits the same workflow and compares its predictions with the hidden measurements. This is the one check of imputation calibration available on real data. It uses no simulation truth.

Usage

catmech_holdout_check(
  fit,
  folds = 5L,
  m = 40L,
  level = 0.9,
  seed = 1L,
  fold_by = c("row", "cluster")
)

Arguments

fit

A `catmech_result` from [catmech_contamination()] or [catmech_reference()].

folds

Number of folds, at least two.

m

Number of imputations per fold refit, at least twenty.

level

Nominal central coverage level, between zero and one.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed. Caller RNG is preserved.

fold_by

`"row"` (default) for stratified row-level cross-validation, or `"cluster"` for cluster-level holdout cross-validation where all reference rows in held-out clusters are hidden together. Requires a clustered fit with `spec$cluster`.

Value

A list with `status`, `summary` (one row of metrics), `rows` (one per held-out reference), `flags`, `failures`, `advice` and `interpretation`. `advice` is nonempty when predictions are no better than the recorded value or the stratum error rate. On two real datasets that happened while `status` stayed clean, and simpler methods did as well or better. It is a reading from that study, not a tested rule.

A list with `status`, `summary`, `rows`, `flags`, `failures`, `advice` and `interpretation`.

Details

Folds are stratified by whether the reference agreed with the recorded value. Reported measures include predictive interval coverage, randomized probability integral transforms, root mean squared error of the model and of the recorded value, and for the contamination model the Brier score against the stratum error rate as well as expected against observed errors. `status` is `miscalibration_detected` when coverage is significantly below nominal, the expected and observed error counts differ at the 1 level. A clean result is not proof of validity: held-out rows share the reference selection process, the check has limited power with few errors, and it does not address nonignorable selection or a reference that is itself wrong.

Examples

set.seed(123)
df <- data.frame(val = stats::rnorm(30, 10, 2), age = stats::rnorm(30, 50, 10))
df$ref <- df$val + stats::rnorm(30, 0, 0.2)
res <- catmech_reference(df, value = "val", reference = "ref", predictors = "age", m = 2, seed = 1)
chk <- catmech_holdout_check(res, folds = 2L, m = 20L, seed = 1L)
print(chk)
#> -- Catmech Holdout Cross-Validation Check --
#> Status:              no_miscalibration_detected
#> Folds completed:     2 (holdout rows: 30, partitioned by: row)
#> Predictive coverage: 0.8333 (nominal: 0.9) (uniform PIT KS p-value: 0.3983)
#> Predictive RMSE:     model = 2.2008 vs recorded = 0.1711
#> Mean interval width: 6.8334
#> Flags:               none
#> 
#> Advice:
#>   * Predictions are no closer to held-out references than the recorded values are.
#>   * Consider catmech_reference(use_recorded = TRUE) or generalized raking.
